MARKET.head: EU greenwashing directive now bans vague eco claims on wine labels
MARKET.summ: New restrictions on environmental marketing claims are putting terms like “natural” and “eco-friendly” under the microscope, prompting questions about what wineries can and can’t include on bottle labels
takeaways: EU Directive 2024/825, known as EmpCo, took enforcement on September 27 and restricts vague environmental claims on consumer products including wine.
Banned claims include generic terms like eco-friendly and green, and sustainability badges without third-party certification.
Enforcement falls to individual member states, with fines up to four percent of annual turnover for widespread violations.

MARKET.head: Bordeaux takes 41% of traded wine value as Burgundy's share jumps
MARKET.summ: Bordeaux strengthened its lead of the market, claiming 41% of traded value. Burgundy’s share also rose compared to last week
takeaways: Bordeaux claimed 41% of the week's traded value on Liv-ex, extending its lead over other regions.
Burgundy's share of traded value rose from 15.7% last week to 20.8%, with DRC and Leflaive leading producers.
Champagne's share fell from 13.0% to 8.5%, while Tuscany's rose to 11.6% led by Soldera and Sassicaia.

MARKET.head: California table grapes stay available through December for holiday promotions
MARKET.summ: Despite an early start to harvest, steady shipments and cold storage supplies are in position to keep California table grapes available for holiday promotions
takeaways: California Table Grape Commission says grapes will remain in promotable volumes throughout December after harvest ends in mid-November.
Commission President Ian LeMay says cold storage and steady shipments keep supply going well past harvest despite an early season start.
Commission consumer research finds 72% of grape purchasers prefer U.S.-grown grapes over imports, which fewer than 5% prefer.

MARKET.head: Bordeaux leads Liv-ex trade with 37.4% share; Lynch-Bages 2005 top-traded
MARKET.summ: US and UK buyers both upped their purchasing, the former segment reclaiming their share of purchasing
takeaways: Bordeaux held the largest share of purchases on the Liv-ex wine trading platform at 37.4%, with Lynch-Bages 2005 the top-traded wine.
Burgundy's share fell to 15.4% from 18.4% the previous week, and Champagne ranked third at 13.0%.
US buyers accounted for 66.2% of Bordeaux's traded value, and their share of overall purchases rose to 9.6% from 7.0%.

MARKET.head: Surrey funds 17 rural projects, including a vineyard bird-repelling laser
MARKET.summ: A wine producer using bird-repelling lasers and cattle farmer using GPS collars to track livestock are among 17 innovative projects funded from a £500,000 pot to boost Surrey’s rural economy. Surrey County Council’s Farming Innovation Accelerator supports farmers and growers with funding for projects to modernise operations,...
takeaways: Surrey County Council's Farming Innovation Accelerator is funding 17 rural and farming projects from a £500,000 pot.
Each recipient receives a grant of up to £35,000 plus expert support, drawn from more than 50 proposals.
Albury Vineyard will install an automated bird-repellent laser to protect 18 acres of grapevines and add over 1,700 bottles yearly.

MARKET.head: Navarra rosado's demanding Saignée method becomes its premium selling point
MARKET.summ: How Navarra Rosado turned production challenges into premium positioning and a compelling marketing story. Andrea Ontiveros Flores, a sommelier and marketing & communications specialist from Alicante, Spain asks if English wine could do the same? Consumers rarely pay more simply because winemaking is difficult.
takeaways: Navarra's Saignée method draws juice for rosé during maceration and can need up to three times more grapes than red production.
Navarra's new Rosado Tradition designation requires the Saignée method and exclusive use of Garnacha.

CULTURE.head: Pembrokeshire's Velfrey wins first Welsh trophy at Glass of Bubbly Awards
CULTURE.summ: Pembrokeshire vineyard wins prestigious Glass of Bubbly trophy and gold medal, plus two silvers, competing against Champagne and sparkling wines from around the world A family-run vineyard in Pembrokeshire has
takeaways: Glass of Bubbly Awards 2026, a London ceremony on 23 October, judged Champagne and sparkling wines blind across categories.
Velfrey Vineyard in Pembrokeshire won gold and the Winter Warmer Trophy for its Cuvée Reserve 2022.
Velfrey's Rhosyn 2023 rosé and NV sparkling wine each took silver, the first Welsh trophy win at the competition.

CULTURE.head: Volcanic soils give wines a distinctive tension, importers and writers say
CULTURE.summ:
Vines on volcanic soil are hard to grow and their grapes are hard-won, but it all combines to produce wines with a very particular sense of place

Good stories need jeopardy. Take The Princess Bride, one of my favourite films, which I recently introduced...
takeaways: Wines from volcanic terroirs share a perceived tension, though volcanic soils vary widely from ash to basalt to pumice.
La Palma producer Victoria Torres Pecis farms black ash soils at 1,200m, with heatwaves, drought and a 2021 eruption during harvest.
Importer Nic Rizzi of Modal Wines says the struggle of growing these vines comes through in the wine.

CULTURE.head: Plumpton College recruits for Level 3 viticulture apprenticeship starting 9 November
CULTURE.summ: Develop the skills your business needs, invest in emerging talent and help shape the future of the UK wine industry with a Viticulture Apprenticeship at Plumpton College. As the UK wine industry continues to grow, developing a skilled workforce is essential to its long-term success. Plumpton College’s Level 3 Viticulture...
takeaways: Plumpton College is recruiting its next Level 3 Viticulture Apprenticeship cohort, commencing 9 November, with late joiners possibly accepted in January.
Qualifications are endorsed by WineGB and combine workplace experience with block weeks of college-based learning at its Wine Centre.
Government funds 100% of training costs for eligible non-levy-paying SMEs' apprentices aged 16 to 24, subject to funding rules.

SCIENCE.head: Enartis advises matching oak alternatives to specific winemaking objectives, not simply adding more oak
SCIENCE.summ: Oak remains one of the most powerful tools available to winemakers for shaping wine style, structure, and complexity. While traditional barrel ageing continues to play an important role, modern oak alternatives offer greater flexibility, lower cost, and increased precision when used with a clearly defined objective.
takeaways: Oak alternatives differ in surface area and toast level, which control how fast and what kind of aromas they release.
Oak chips added during active fermentation barely aid colour stability, since oxygen is very scarce then.
Colour stability gains come mainly during maturation, when oak is combined with controlled oxygen such as micro-oxygenation.

SCIENCE.head: English vineyards see early harvests and heat damage after 2026 heatwaves
SCIENCE.summ: With harvest complete, or nearing completion on many vineyards, Hutchinsons agronomists Rob Saunders and Will Robinson look at the impact of the record-breaking summer and what we can learn for future seasons. While 2026 could be remembered as a vintage season for some growers, others will look back less fondly, having first...
takeaways: English vineyards faced late May frost, then repeated heatwaves and drought in 2026, with 54 Met Office stations setting daily records.
Harvest came 10-14 days early, with Sauvignon Blanc ripening well while Bacchus struggled under intense heat and UV.
Viticulturist Markus Keller says photosynthesis falls sharply once leaf temperatures reach 40-45°C, and brief extreme heat is worse than prolonged warmth.

SCIENCE.head: UK vineyards navigate early, warm, dry 2026 harvest after frost
SCIENCE.summ: After a run of dramatically different vintages, 2026 has given UK viticulture another season that challenged assumptions, but also demonstrated just how much English and Welsh vineyards can achieve. The 2026 growing season began with a series of extraordinary frost events, creating a challenging start before developing into a...
takeaways: A 2026 growing season in England and Wales began with severe frost, then turned warm and dry with rapid ripening.
Harvest arrived several weeks early at some vineyards, while dry weather kept disease pressure manageable and fruit clean.
The author argues growers must build resilience yearly through soil health, water management, and clone and variety choice.

SCIENCE.head: Domaine Bousquet details organic and water-saving practices at Mendoza winery
SCIENCE.summ: Domaine Bousquet continues to elevate Argentine wine through generations of dedication and innovation in organic wine practices. Earlier this year, Irma Remigio and her team warmly welcomed SWR’s Membership Manager, Ilva Fridenberga, to their winery. The winery, located at the foot of the Andes Mountains, is globally recognized...
takeaways: SWR membership manager Ilva Fridenberga visited Domaine Bousquet's Mendoza winery at the foot of the Andes in February.
The winery is trialing biodiversity and garden vineyard corridors, harvesting from outside vine rows in the biodiversity corridors.
It switched to high-pressure hoses for cleaning harvest boxes, using significantly less water, and is a signatory of the Bottle Weight Accord.

SCIENCE.head: Grenache rootstocks and irrigation shape water use and stomatal control in Spain
SCIENCE.summ: Under the context of global change, any decrease in water use by crops is essential, because water is becoming a more and more scarce resource, especially in Mediterranean areas, where grapevines are grown
takeaways: A three-year NE Spain study compared Grenache on three rootstocks, irrigated and non-irrigated, to measure water use.
Non-irrigated vines had higher water use efficiency, and 110-R and 41-B outperformed 161-49 on that measure.
Stomatal conductance differences from irrigation persisted all season, with hormonal signals likely driving stomatal control under these conditions.

SCIENCE.head: Italian researchers outline viticulture strategies for climate change and biodiversity
SCIENCE.summ: In the globalization conditions possible future scenarios, optimistic and pessimistic are supposed
takeaways: A Pisa University paper addresses future viticulture under climate change, water scarcity and market competition.
It proposes genetic improvement and preserving local grape varieties, with Italian regions starting recovery projects for local varieties.
Field trials on Lazio's Malvasia, Cesanese d'Affile and Cabernet Sauvignon used the Cordon Spur of Conegliano training system.

SCIENCE.head: Portuguese trial cuts Loureiro and Borraçal yields with Ethephon and thinning
SCIENCE.summ: Some years, climate conditions and biological events increment the fertility of vines, which can lead to over cropping and a decrease of wine quality
takeaways: A 2007 Vinhos Verdes trial tested Ethephon, Prohexadione-calcium and manual bunch thinning on Loureiro and Borraçal vines.
Manual thinning cut Borraçal yield about 41% and Loureiro about 26% against untreated controls.
Ethephon at berry buckshot size raised Loureiro sugar and lowered acidity, while Borraçal gained no quality benefit.

SCIENCE.head: Vine balance concept and how it shifts across the growing season
SCIENCE.summ: Vine balance is a commonly used term in viticulture that expresses the concept of an appropriate balance of vegetative to reproductive growth of the vine
takeaways: Vine balance describes the appropriate ratio of vegetative growth to reproductive growth in a grapevine.
A balanced vine ripens its crop, sets fruitful buds for next year, and builds reserves without excessive canopy growth.
A dynamic carbohydrate simulation model can track seasonal vegetative and reproductive demands against canopy carbon supply.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Vinho Verde: Quinta da Pegadinha
NEWSLETTERS.summ: This is a small family vineyard and farm 15 km from the ocean, in the southern part of Vinho Verde,
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jamie Goode
takeaways: Quinta da Pegadinha is a small family vineyard and farm on the Cavado river in southern Vinho Verde, with 6 hectares of vines.
Winemaker Felipe Lemos says the estate is not organic because organic maize feed for its cows is too difficult to source.
Reviewed wines include Peghadinha Reserva Branco 2022 (94/100), Alvarinho Reserva 2023 (93/100) and Padeiro Grande Escolha 2023 (92/100).

NEWSLETTERS.summ: Hello and welcome to my weekly dig through the pile of wine samples that show up on my doorstep, asking

NEWSLETTERS.head: Albarino? Soleri? Pinot Iskra? New White Wine Player in China
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Attendees of the China Sommelier Summit in Shanghai were treated to a new local white wine producer pouring smack dab in the middle of the
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jim Boyce
takeaways: Lan Yue, established in Yantai in 2021, poured six wines at the China Sommelier Summit in Shanghai, including Albarino, Chardonnay, Viognier, Pinot Iskra and Soleri.
Lan Yue planted its first vines in 2023 and recently released its first wines, with its Albarino singled out as a standout.
The winery's vineyards cover about 230 mu (15.5 hectares), including 40 mu (2.7 hectares) of Albarino, in Penglai, Shandong province.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Essential Kit for Kitchen Season
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Outfitting your kitchen with the season’s essential tools, plus this week’s favorite stories about food, wine, and culture
NEWSLETTERS.author: Meg Maker
takeaways: Meg Maker's Maker's Table piece frames late autumn as "Kitchen Season", when cooking becomes a way to mark occasions.
The clocks drop back on Sunday, Oct 30, 2026, bringing darkness an hour sooner.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Tasting Diaries: October 2026
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Niagara’s Cabernet Franc harvest finally gets underway, plus the bottles that made my October memorable
NEWSLETTERS.author: Cab Franc Chronicles
takeaways: Buttonwood Grove's 2025 Blanc de Franc from the Finger Lakes is a semi-sweet white Cabernet Franc, which the reviewer would call off-dry, with about 10 g/L residual sugar.
Château de Fosse Sèche's 2018 Éolithe VDF from Saumur is grown on Jurassic silex de Brossay limestone and is described as still having 5+ years of life ahead.
Fogolar Wines' 2018 Cabernet Franc Picone Vineyard, from VQA Vinemount Ridge in Niagara, comes from vines planted in the early 1980s by viticulturalist Phil Clarke and winemaker Marc Pistor.

NEWSLETTERS.head: A New White Zin
NEWSLETTERS.summ: If you are not familiar with the lore of White Zinfandel , America’s greatest contribution to wine culture , you are missing out on some excellent cocktail conversation. I understand this might sound like the layup for a bad wine joke, but I’m not being facetious. White Zinfandel is as important to the United States
NEWSLETTERS.author: Tim Atkin MW
takeaways: Tim Atkin argues the US wine industry needs a 'new' White Zinfandel, a cheap, accessible category to revive demand.
He cites US drinkers consuming 49.2 million bottles of White Zinfandel in 2024 despite wine sales being at an all-time low.
Atkin proposes 'Relevé', a field blend of red and white grapes across an estate or region, inspired by The Feudal Project's Mrs. Crabtree's field blend made by Will Marengo.

NEWSLETTERS.head: A deeper look at underwater wine aging
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Is a wine from the depths ‘better’ or does it depend on the boat?
NEWSLETTERS.author: Miquel Hudin
takeaways: Attis, a winery owned by the Fariña family near Pontevedra, Galicia, ages magnums of its Albariño underwater in the O Grove estuary.
The underwater-aged Attis Albariño 'Mar' is aged five months at 13-16C and is compared against the 'Standard' bottling, which is about 120,000 bottles a year.
The author's past tastings of underwater-aged wines found them more advanced and tired than land-aged counterparts, leaving the practice's value in doubt.

NEWSLETTERS.head: What to Know Before This Year’s Hospices de Beaune Wine Auction
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Discover the world's most famous charity wine auction held since 1859. Get essential tips and insights for this year's legendary Burgundy event
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jonathan Finch
takeaways: The 166th Hospices de Beaune wine sale takes place Sunday 15 November 2026 under the Halles de Beaune, with the first lot around 2.30pm.
The 2026 vintage is a small crop of 432 barrels, 348 red and 84 white, with the low yield caused by an early heatwave.
Last year's sale raised €18.8 million, with reds averaging €27,480 and whites €58,580 per cask, and Grand Crus averaging €86,290.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Visiting the Vineyard in the Sky
NEWSLETTERS.summ: The extraordinary story of Domaine de Beudon in Valais, Switzerland
NEWSLETTERS.author: Simon J. Woolf
takeaways: Domaine de Beudon, a Valais estate at 890 metres, is run by the Granges-Faiss family, reachable only by cable car or a 90-minute hike.
Jacky Granges-Faiss bought the estate in 1971; Demeter certification came in 1992, making it Valais's first certified estate.
Since 2016, Marion Granges-Faiss has been the de facto winemaker after Jacky died, though the wines are still partly made at Pierre-Antoine Crettenand's Saillon winery.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Yet Another Vintage Port Flex Post (Tasting Selections From 1985 - 2022)
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Last week, I published a bunch of reviews from an NYC media tasting of selections from the (stellar) 2024 Port vintage. I typically follow those type of posts up with another post of other, older selections of vintage Ports that I tasted at the same event, and I offer them without much shame as simply […] This article was...
NEWSLETTERS.author: Joe Roberts
takeaways: 1WineDude published reviews from an NYC media tasting of selections from the 2024 Port vintage.
A follow-up post covers older vintage Ports tasted at the same event.
